new_statements.quote: ... some of the Upper Cross and Bendi languages have three level tonemes. Gliding tones and phonemic downstepped high tones are common throughout the subbranch. At least some languages of every group for which instrumental or impressionistic data are available have different types of stress and/or accent systems co-occurring and interacting with both tonal and intonational systems. Typical stress patterns involve the parsing of utterances into phonological phrases over which a single stress (peak of pitch, duration, and/or perceived loudness) falls, the pragmatically or grammatically controlled emphasis ...

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: statement check: group-level-statement. Faraclas 1989 handbook chapter generalises over the Cross River sub-branch ('some of the Upper Cross and Bendi languages have three level tonemes.. at least some languages of every group.. have stress and/or accent systems'); Obanliku appears only in the classification list p.382 and no Obanliku data are cited. the compiler already says so; family-level only. | checker: Faraclas 1989 'Cross River' in Bendor-Samuel (ed.): archive.org item nigercongolangua0000unse exists (controlled lending = login, correct). A's saved file is a snippet transcript, not the book; I re-verified the passage independently with two fresh archive.org full-text queries through…
new_statements.relation_note: Sub-branch is tonal (2-3 level tonemes, contour tones, downstep); some languages additionally have phrase-level stress/accent interacting with tone. Full chapter not opened (archive.org controlled lending = login; Google Books no preview; UPA volume print).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Family-level: Cross River languages in Faraclas's sense (incl. the Bendi group, of which Obanliku is a member) are tonal with level tonemes -- some Upper Cross and Bendi languages have three levels (the others, by implication of the preceding clause not recovered, two) -- plus gliding tones and phonemic downstepped high 'throughout the subbranch'. Nothing is asserted of Obanliku individually.
new_statements.exceptions: Stress/accent: 'at least some languages of every group for which.. data are available' have stress/accent systems interacting with tone; the typical pattern is one stress per phonological phrase (phrase-level prominence), i.e. hedged and not attributable to Obanliku, for which no data are cited.
new_statements.identity_note: PASS-1 WORK, added: the sub-branch tone/stress statement itself (pass 1 saw only an Upper Cross snippet and left it 'family-level at best, unopened'). Recovered verbatim from overlapping Google Books feed snippets (vol. HsdkAAAAMAAJ) and archive.org full-text highlights (item nigercongolangua0000unse, page 389). The passage generalises over 'Upper Cross and Bendi languages' -- Faraclas's Bendi group explicitly includes the Obanliku chain (Basang, Bebi, Bishiri, Bisu, Busi) on p. 382 -- but Obanliku is NOT named in the tone passage (index: 'Obanliku, 382' only). Family-level, not a first-hand Obanliku description.
